newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firm on dollar inflow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firm on dollar inflow.

text.p: Mexican peso contracts recovered from their mixed stance in earlier trade to end firmer for the fourth session in a row on Thursday due to capital flows into Mexico.
"Players have discounted good inflation data, but dollars are still flowing into the market," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended trade 1.3 and 1.8 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8090/7.8120 and 7.8200/7.8230 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had closed trade for the day 1.8 centavos firmer at 7.8200/7.8230 per dollar.

Banco de Mexico announced after the close of trade that consumer prices rose 0.48 percent during the first half of July. This compares with an average increase of 0.49 percent forecast by 12 financial firms in a prior Reuters survey MEX22.
The Mexican bourse was up 31.61 points in late trade to 4,773.73 on foreign buying, dealers said.
"The market is long on dollars, dealers stay with them because demand is so weak," the trader added.
But other dealers said selling dollars could still be good business if the market anticipated further peso strength and forecast the peso could gain more ground during trade on Friday.
